clue.text: Writer takes walk to meadow, flanked by birds

parts.note: a step is a single pace of walking

indicators.note: flanked by means having something on each side, so the two birds sit either side of the meadow

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a cock is a male bird
a lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: An author goes for a stroll to a field surrounded by birds.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'birds', supplies two pieces that sit either side of the meadow. Stephen Leacock was a Canadian humorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Leacock was a Canadian humorist and author, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Problematical situation to bore chaps in group half slouching around?

indicators.note: in places the three run-together pieces within the group word

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
a mire is a difficult situation one is stuck in
to tire someone is to bore them
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A muddled sentence about a gang of men lounging about.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: someone partly retired is only half lounging about, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has partly stopped working spends some of their time at leisure, a whimsical take on partial retirement.

clue.text: See problem when one enters blessed place

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city and see in England

indicators.note: enters says the numeral goes into the problem word

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Look at a difficulty as someone arrives at a holy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a bishop's see, here ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Elysium was the paradise where the blessed lived after death.

clue.text: The horrible situation 'e put up with on account of Lily?

parts.note: hell is a dreadful situation
'e is a dropped-h spelling of he, giving just the letter E
bore, the past tense of bear, means put up with

explanation.surface: A man complains about a dreadful state he tolerated because of a woman called Lily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a woman's name; it stands for a plant, the question mark admitting that false hellebore belongs to the lily group.
explanation.definitionFit: The false hellebore (Veratrum) is a plant of the lily family, so the plant name loosely fits a lily.

clue.text: Phony language not what you get in the silly season?

definitions.meaning: in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, the deceptive official language of the Party

definitions.text: not what you get in the silly season?
definitions.meaning: the silly season is the quiet summer when newspapers lack stories, so it is no high point for reports

explanation.surface: Fake jargon is not what summer newspapers deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, NEWS PEAK: the silly season, the British summer lull when papers print trivia, is the opposite of a peak in news.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell coined the term for the Party's distorting official language, now used of any deceptive jargon.

clue.text: Princess who works as a secretary in Brussels?

parts.note: Brussels hosts the EU institutions, so euro- prefixes things European
a PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A royal lady takes an office job at the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, hence EURO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Europa was a Phoenician princess carried off by Zeus disguised as a bull.

clue.text: Valley searched thoroughly, endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: combed means searched carefully through

explanation.surface: Someone scoured a valley without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' seems to say the search went on and on; it removes the D at the end of COMBED.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short valley or hollow, especially in southern England.

clue.text: Arrive without vessel for dessert

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so arrive goes round the vessel

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: Turn up with no bowl for the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Compote is fruit stewed in syrup, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Body tissue that's reconstituted in the lad's clone

indicators.note: reconstituted means put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some flesh grown again in a boy's genetic copy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all of IN THE LADS CLONE, including the S of lad's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscles to the heel bone, a piece of the body's connective tissue.

clue.text: Ship won't necessarily flourish

definitions.meaning: the vessel that took the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620
read as two words, a plant that may bloom, which is not certain to

explanation.surface: A vessel isn't sure to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MAY FLOWER: something that may flower won't necessarily do so.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims from Plymouth to New England in 1620, a famous sailing vessel.

clue.text: Make fun of operatic character getting caught

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Mocking a character from opera who has been nabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to imitate someone, often in order to ridicule them.

clue.text: Listener (going back) seen as home for fashionable poet

indicators.note: seen as home for says the listener word houses the fashionable word
going back means the listener word is read backwards

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A hearer returns to find a residence for a stylish poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns the listener round to RAE. Craig Raine is an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Craig Raine is a contemporary English poet, founder of the Martian school of poetry.

clue.text: Food pioneer found out, keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the reworked letters hold the musical mark
found out suggests exposure but here signals the letters being worked out afresh

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A food innovator was exposed while keeping very quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' looks like exposure but rearranges the letters of pioneer into a food word that splits to hold the musical mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-style salami, a common pizza topping.

clue.text: Material in test given to secretary?

indicators.note: given to means the test word is added onto the secretary word

parts.note: a temp is a temporary secretary
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Cloth in an exam handed to an office worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun meaning fabric; it is an adjective meaning worldly, not spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal and material both mean belonging to this world rather than the spiritual realm.

clue.text: Big bird is "bony"

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for big
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A large bird is skinny.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a crossword convention for big.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is the technical word for relating to or made of bone.

clue.text: Was lazier than the Piggy-wig in tree?

definitions.text: Was lazier than the Piggy-wig in tree?

parts.words: Was lazier than the Piggy-wig in tree?
parts.note: in Lear's The Owl and the Pussy-cat, a Piggy-wig stood in a wood; someone lazier would have taken a seat in that wood, which split differently names a tree

explanation.surface: Was someone idler than the pig in Edward Lear's poem?
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's nonsense poem has 'there in a wood a Piggy-wig stood'. Not standing but sitting in a wood is lazier, and the phrase run together is a tropical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a tropical tree prized for its glossy, satin-like timber.

clue.text: I made waves about hospital department providing for mental illness

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go round the department
made waves suggests causing trouble; here waves signals the letters moving into a new order

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: I caused a fuss over a hospital unit offering psychiatric care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made waves' reads as causing a fuss, but 'waves' alone rearranges I MADE into a word that is split open.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is a chronic decline in memory and reasoning, a disorder of the mind.

clue.text: Part of firework display with music out of this world

parts.note: rock is a genre of music
ET is the extraterrestrial, from beyond our world

explanation.surface: A firework show with otherworldly music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' looks like praise; it means an alien, ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is a firework that shoots into the sky before bursting.

clue.text: Behold musical band going round that capital city

indicators.note: going round means the band word encircles the behold word

parts.note: a combo is a small band of musicians
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Look, a band is touring that city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link word; the musical band is split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the commercial capital and former official capital of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Make contact with head to establish suitability

parts.note: to meet someone is to make contact with them
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's place names

explanation.surface: Get in touch with the boss to check whether one is fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a boss; it is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Meetness is an old word for being fit or proper, from meet meaning suitable.

clue.text: Man buried under his female ancestor's town

indicators.note: buried under means the man's name is placed below the ancestor in this down entry

parts.note: Eve is the first woman, every man's female ancestor
Ham is a son of Noah in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man is buried beneath a grandmother's town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' means after. EVESHAM is a market town in Worcestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham is a market town in Worcestershire, England.

clue.text: Yapper's joke about sailors capsizing

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is just yapper

indicators.note: about means the joke word goes round the turned sailors

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: capsizing turns the sailors upside down, which in a down entry reads them upwards

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors

explanation.surface: A chatterbox's quip about seamen going over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' turns the sailors round to SBA. 'Yapper's' is 'yapper is', the 's a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is someone who talks endlessly, just like a yapper.

clue.text: Improve, having married priest — nothing to reprove

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
O looks like zero, nothing
to rate someone is an old use meaning to scold them

explanation.surface: Make things better, as a wed cleric with no reason to scold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing to reprove' looks like a single idea; it is O and RATE, an old verb meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To meliorate is to make better, the root of ameliorate.

clue.text: In corn I see the region's birds

indicators.note: In says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Among the corn, I see the local birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornis is the term for the bird life of a particular region, its avifauna.

clue.text: Family member pleasant, full of energy

indicators.note: full of means the pleasant word holds the energy letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A relative who is nice and lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, a relative.

clue.text: Classical name sending message from the ladies' circle?

definitions.meaning: in ancient Rome, a person's clan name
an all-female group would send word that men are not wanted

explanation.surface: A women's club sends out a notice in a Latin name.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO MEN, a ladies-only group's message. In Rome the nomen was the family name, as Julius in Gaius Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: The nomen was the middle, clan name of a Roman citizen, so a classical name.

clue.text: The debtor somehow under an obligation to settle?

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A person who owes money is bound to pay up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' looks like paying a debt; here it means settling down in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged has pledged to marry, so is bound to settle down.

clue.text: Screams on a tug'd send us scurrying?

definitions.text: Screams on a tug'd send us scurrying?

indicators.note: scurrying means rushing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Cries from a tugboat would have rescuers rushing out.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SCREAMS ON A TUG'D gives the answer, and the whole clue describes them racing to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the coastguard respond to cries of distress at sea, so the whole clue describes them.
